stories.head: Salesforce Launches Koa, Its First CRM Reasoning Model Built on NVIDIA Nemotron
stories.plain: Salesforce and NVIDIA have released Koa, a CRM-native reasoning model trained on 27 years of Salesforce data. Unlike generic LLMs, Koa is designed to handle complex, multi-step enterprise tasks inside CRM workflows. It also brings NVIDIA's open models into regulated-sector deployments via Missionforce. This directly changes how agentic AI gets bought and embedded in sales and marketing stacks.

stories.head: Agentic AI Is Actively Running Media Buys — and Governance Is the Real Challenge Now
stories.plain: Autonomous systems are already executing real-time bidding decisions and mid-flight budget shifts with minimal human approval. This analysis argues the frontier question is no longer capability but responsible control — who sets guardrails, who is liable, and how marketers audit autonomous spend decisions. Essential framing for anyone buying or governing AI-driven media.

stories.head: Adform Becomes OpenAI Technology Partner as ChatGPT Ads Roll Out Across Europe
stories.plain: OpenAI is extending its ChatGPT Ads platform into Europe with Adform as an official technology partner, giving Adform clients programmatic access to ad placements inside ChatGPT. This matters because it signals AI answer environments becoming formal paid media channels, reshaping how marketers think about both media buying and generative engine visibility.

stories.head: Cordial Research: Holiday Shoppers Already Using AI Assistants for Product Discovery and Deal Hunting
stories.plain: New consumer research from Cordial shows shoppers are actively turning to AI assistants for product discovery and price comparison ahead of the holiday season. Brands that fail to show up in AI-generated answers — or that can't deliver trusted, personalized value — risk losing consideration entirely. Concrete evidence that GEO and personalization strategies are now business-critical.

stories.head: Lokalise Launches Vantage: No-Code AI Workspace for Localizing Marketing Campaigns at Scale
stories.plain: Lokalise's Vantage is a no-code localization workspace built specifically for marketing teams, embedding AI-powered translation and adaptation directly into existing campaign tools for websites, creative assets, and documents. Launching end of September, it matters because it lowers the barrier to multilingual personalization — a key bottleneck for brands running AI-driven content at global scale.

stories.head: Salesforce Launches Koa, First CRM Reasoning Model Built on NVIDIA Nemotron
stories.plain: Salesforce and NVIDIA jointly launched Koa, a CRM-native reasoning model trained on 27 years of Salesforce data. It handles complex, multi-step enterprise tasks inside Salesforce's agentic stack. This matters because it marks a shift from general-purpose AI bolted onto CRM to a purpose-built reasoning layer that can act — not just answer — within customer workflows.

stories.head: Agentic AI Is Already Running Real-Time Media Buying With Minimal Human Sign-Off
stories.plain: A practitioner analysis explains how autonomous agents are now executing bids, reallocating budgets mid-campaign, and adjusting targeting with little human approval at each step. This is no longer experimental — it's live. The piece focuses on what responsible deployment looks like, making it essential reading for anyone buying or governing paid media with AI.

stories.head: Adform Becomes OpenAI Tech Partner as ChatGPT Ads Expand Into Europe
stories.plain: OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Ads in Europe and Adform is one of its first official platform partners, meaning Adform clients can now serve ads inside ChatGPT. This is a concrete step toward AI-answer environments becoming a paid media channel — directly reshaping where marketing budgets flow and how brands stay visible in generative search.

stories.head: Cordial Research: Holiday Shoppers Turn to AI Assistants for Discovery but Demand Personalized Value
stories.plain: New consumer research shows that shoppers are actively using AI assistants for product discovery and deal-finding during the holiday season, but they won't convert unless experiences feel personally relevant and trustworthy. This data is directly actionable for teams planning Q4 campaigns and deciding how much to invest in AI-driven personalization versus broad reach.

stories.head: Talkdesk Launches In-Store Commerce Orchestration to Unify Retail Customer Data
stories.plain: Talkdesk for Stores connects in-store, digital, and contact-center touchpoints into a single unified customer view for retailers. It lets associates and automated systems act on the same data in real time. For retail marketers, this closes a major gap between physical and digital engagement and enables AI-driven decisions that are actually grounded in complete customer context.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: Agentic AI Moves from Concept to Commerce Infrastructure
body: Agentic AI — systems that plan, decide, and act autonomously — is no longer a roadmap item. Media buying, CRM reasoning (Salesforce's Koa), and venue sales automation (MomentusMAX) all launched production-ready agentic layers this month, meaning budget-allocation and pipeline decisions are increasingly being delegated to machines in real time.

The decision that changes for marketers is no longer 'should we pilot AI?' but 'which workflows do we still own, and which do we hand over?' Tools like RSVPify's MCP connector show the pattern spreading even into niche verticals, compressing the timeline for every team to answer that question.
ev: MarTech Series · Salesforce Koa CRM model

themes.head: AI Enters Conversational Advertising at Scale
body: OpenAI's ChatGPT Ads launching in Europe — with Adform as an early platform partner — marks a structural shift in paid media: ad inventory now lives inside AI conversations, not just alongside content. Holiday-shopper research from Cordial simultaneously shows consumers are already comfortable letting AI assistants influence purchases, provided trust signals are present.

For planners, this collapses the distinction between 'search,' 'social,' and 'AI assistant' channels into a single intent layer. Budgets, creative formats, and measurement frameworks built for traditional placements need rethinking before the next major shopping season.
ev: Agile Brand · ChatGPT Ads in Europe
Agile Brand · Holiday shoppers & AI trust

themes.head: CX Platforms Double Down on AI-Driven Orchestration
body: Three separate CX moves this month — Talkdesk's commerce orchestration on the retail floor, Merlin Entertainments deploying NiCE CXone globally, and SupportNinja's MomentumLabs lab unit — all point in the same direction: customer experience is being re-engineered around AI orchestration layers rather than point tools. Medallia's recognition as the sole leader in customer feedback management reinforces that unified data pipelines underpin the whole stack.

The strategic implication is vendor consolidation. Brands that still run fragmented point solutions for chat, feedback, and commerce risk being outpaced by competitors whose AI orchestrator has a full-signal view of every customer touchpoint.

themes.head: AI Trust Gap: Verification & Fraud as the Hidden Tax
body: Two risk stories surfaced this month that sit beneath the hype: HYPR found that nearly all fraudulent hires obtain active corporate credentials before detection, a threat amplified by AI-generated identities; ChatOn responded to a parallel consumer trust problem by shipping a dedicated fact-checking feature. Trust is becoming a product feature, not just a brand value.

For MarTech and AI buyers, this means procurement and security teams must be in the room when new AI tools are evaluated. The cost of a credential breach or a viral AI hallucination now rivals the cost of slow adoption — making verification infrastructure a competitive necessity, not a compliance checkbox.
ev: Agile Brand · HYPR fraudulent hires research

themes.head: No-Code AI Tools Democratise Global Content at Speed
body: Lokalise's Vantage workspace and Conga's AiMe contract-intelligence tool both launched this month as explicitly no-code environments, letting marketers and ops teams deploy AI for localisation and document workflows without engineering queues. Achievers Intelligence similarly packages workforce recognition data into self-serve insight dashboards.

The pattern signals a second wave of AI adoption: the first wave required data-science resources; this wave hands capability directly to the people who understand the business problem. Teams that embrace these no-code layers now will compound advantage rapidly over those waiting for IT-led rollouts.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — media buying, CX orchestration, content localisation, and identity security — AI is shifting from an experiment brands run to infrastructure brands run on, and the teams that treat it as such now will set the competitive baseline for everyone else.
